## Why
rebar's mutating verbs follow the classic Unix rule of silence: `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `tag`, `edit`, `set-file-impact` exit 0 with empty stdout on success (only `create`/`revert`/`claim` print, because they return generated state). Observed operational cost (2026-08-14, bug clubby-circular-halicore): success and silent idempotent no-op are indistinguishable on stdout (failure is already distinguishable — nonzero exit + stderr — but agents don't trust silence), so agents routinely run a second `rebar show` to verify their own write — an extra store read per mutation — and one agent misread a silent success as a failed write, filed a spurious bug, and retried the identical command. Modern CLI practice (clig.dev; kubectl/git/gh/terraform) prints a one-line confirmation of every state change. rebar's primary operators are agents that must confirm their writes; the confirmation belongs in the mutation's own output.

## Scope
- **IN**: the silent write verbs = `_WRITES_FULL` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:125 — create, idea, comment, link, unlink, revert, edit, tag, untag, archive, set-file-impact, set-verify-commands, attach-commits, session-log) plus the `_LIFECYCLE` mutators (:114 — transition, reopen, claim). Verbs in these sets that already print (`create`, `idea`, `revert`, `claim`, `transition`, `session-log`) KEEP THEIR EXISTING OUTPUT VERBATIM — scripts consume those lines; no normalization in this ticket.
- **OUT**: MCP tools (structured outputSchemas already confirm), doctor/fsck/compact/bridge/tracker-maintenance (own reporting), any config-key equivalent of --quiet.

## Plan
1. **Uniform message contract.** Success: one stdout line `<past-tense-verb> <args-summary>` built ONLY from CLI arguments + the write seam's outcome (no follow-up store read/reduce): `linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `unlinked <src> -/-> <target> (<relation>)`, `comment added to <alias>`, `tagged <alias>: +<tag>`, `untagged <alias>: -<tag>`, `edited <alias>: <fields>`, `impact set on <alias>: <n> paths`, `archived <alias>`, `verify-commands set on <alias>: <n>`, `commits attached to <alias>: <n>`, `reopened <alias>: closed -> open`. No-op (where the seam reports one): `no change: <specific reason>` — e.g. `no change: already linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `no change: tag <tag> already on <alias>`. Exit 0 both ways.
2. **Per-verb outcome signal, existing contracts preserved.** The executor confirms each core seam's ACTUAL return contract before touching it (Serena find_referencing_symbols + grep for string refs) and extends compatibly:
   - Seams returning `None` with no consumers gain a small outcome return (wrote/noop + detail).
   - Seams whose return IS consumed — e.g. `add_dependency` returns `dict | None` (the REDIRECT record), which `link_core` propagates and the MCP/library facade consumes — are NOT changed; the CLI derives the confirmation from what the seam already exposes, adding a parallel channel (e.g. a second return element via a new wrapper, or an out-param dataclass) ONLY if the existing signal cannot distinguish wrote-vs-noop, and never altering the existing consumed value's type or meaning.
   - Verbs with no idempotent no-op path (e.g. `comment` always writes) get success lines only; the inventory table in the change documents each verb's classification.
3. **Global `--quiet`/`-q` pre-extracted at the top-level router** (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py) BEFORE any partition dispatch — this is required because the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaf verbs (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) treat any option-looking token as a usage error and never call parse_output. Pre-extraction strips the flag from argv once, for every verb, uniformly. `--quiet` suppresses confirmation lines only; errors/exit codes untouched.
4. **Channel discipline:** confirmations print only in default text mode. Where a verb supports the existing structured output convention (`--output json` / `-o` via parse_output), stdout remains exclusively the JSON document; the outcome rides as a structured field (`"outcome": "<verb-past>"|"noop"`). Verbs without an --output mode are unaffected.
5. **stdout/stderr split:** confirmations to stdout (the command's result); warnings/logs stay on stderr. Exit codes unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every verb in `_WRITES_FULL` + `_LIFECYCLE` that is silent today prints the step-1 success line on a successful write; per-verb tests assert the exact line and that no additional store read/reduce builds it (call-count or monkeypatch assertion on the reduce path).
- [ ] Every verb whose seam reports an idempotent no-op prints the `no change: ...` form, exits 0, writes no event (store-event count asserted); the change includes the inventory table classifying each verb (no-op-capable vs always-writes), and re-link of an identical active edge is among the tested no-ops.
- [ ] Already-printing verbs' existing stdout is byte-identical before/after (golden assertions for create/claim/revert/transition outputs).
- [ ] Consumed seam returns are unchanged: `add_dependency`'s `dict | None` REDIRECT contract and its `link_core`/facade consumers verified untouched by tests that exercise the REDIRECT path.
- [ ] `--quiet`/`-q` works on every in-scope verb including the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaves (tested on at least comment + tag), suppressing only the confirmation; under `--output json` stdout stays a single valid JSON document with the outcome field (tested).
- [ ] Confirmations on stdout, logs on stderr (captured-stream tests); existing exit-code contract tests stay green.
- [ ] docs/user-guide.md + cli-reference regenerated; `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
